summary: Coos County, OR ground lookout (Bill's Butte): CCC cab 1938, Aircraft Warning post 1942, 1962 replacement; register says removed 1967, state inventory still lists it in 1974-77.

facts.design: L-4 cab built by the CCC in 1938 as a ground cabin; 14x14 ft ground house in 1962 (register says Amort cab)
facts.status_note: Gone. Register gives removal in 1967 but state inventory still listed it as a secondary lookout in 1977; no source describes the summit today.

staffing.status: Manned by the Coos Fire Patrol from 1939; staffed full time in 1948; secondary observation point by 1974

facts.agency: Coos Fire Patrol (Coos County FPA), later the Oregon Department of Forestry per the register

events.note: Standard lookout cabin built by the Camp McKinley CCC; the register describes an L-4 cab on the ground
Manned by Ned Baker of Marshfield in July 1939
Activated for the Aircraft Warning Service on March 9, 1942; a 10-by-12-foot sleeping quarters was under construction by September 1942
Staffed full time in 1948; staffing cost $561.00
Old lookout torn down after the 1961 fire season
14-by-14-foot ground house built at a cost of $3,469 (district report); register says an Amort cab
Reactivated after two years out of use to watch an area where incendiary fires had been reported
Register gives 1967 as the removal date for the Amort cab; the state inventory still listed the lookout as a secondary observation point in 1974 and as a secondary lookout in 1977
Classified as a secondary lookout in March 1977

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1967 as the removal year. A 1965 newspaper item says the lookout was reactivated, and state inventory entries from 1974 and 1977 still list it as a secondary point, so 1967 cannot be confirmed. The story gives the register date and flags the conflict rather than picking one.

The register says the 1962 replacement was an Amort cab, while the district annual report and Fire Lookout both describe a 14-by-14-foot ground house. A 1961 newspaper item also mentions a new tower. The story follows the district report and notes the register's version.
A 1938 article puts the site eight miles southeast of Bandon; a 1939 article puts it ten miles. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: The 1938 to 1962 history is well sourced from newspapers and district reports. The register's removal date (1967) conflicts with state inventory entries from 1974 and 1977, and the 1962 replacement type is disputed. The story flags both. The 1942 survey description was written about the summit building and is quoted through the Forest Lookouts page; I did not open the federal datasheet itself. Nothing we read describes the summit today. The site is called Bill's Butte in the newspapers and Bill Peak in the register and on USGS maps.
